parts.name: Raspberry Pi AI HAT+ 2 with Hailo-10H and 8GB RAM
parts.software_stack: Hailo software suite / Raspberry Pi AI stack
parts.plain_language: One of the cleanest low-power accelerator candidates because it combines dedicated model memory, a shipping generative-AI software path and extremely low accelerator power. The 8GB memory ceiling keeps it in the small-LLM/VLM specialist role rather than making it a replacement for 64GB Ryzen workers.
parts.source_notes: Raspberry Pi lists the AI HAT+ 2 at US$200 with 8GB onboard RAM and Hailo-10H. Hailo lists 40 TOPS INT4 / 20 TOPS INT8 and 2.5W typical chip power. Power is accelerator-only, not Raspberry Pi 5 system power.

parts.name: Firefly Core-1688JD4 BM1688 SoM, 8GB RAM / 32GB storage
parts.memory_type: LPDDR4/LPDDR4X family; current store SKU advertises 8GB RAM
parts.plain_language: BM1688 is interesting because SOPHGO maintains an actual LLM/VLM deployment stack rather than leaving us to infer usefulness from TOPS. The module can act more like a tiny standalone AI computer than a dumb PCIe card, although its memory size still limits model scale.
parts.source_notes: Firefly store snapshot showed US$339 for the 8GB/32GB SoM. SOPHGO LLM-TPU explicitly supports BM1688 with Qwen, Llama, DeepSeek and multimodal models.

parts.name: SOPHGO BM1684X development board, 16GB LPDDR4X class
parts.plain_language: The price is not attractive yet, but BM1684X earns a place because it has 16GB of local memory and an actively maintained LLM compiler/runtime with multi-chip support. It is a software-compatibility reference we can use while hunting much cheaper used or direct-China BM1684X systems.
parts.source_notes: Observed reseller price US$914.12. SOPHGO ecosystem references describe BM1684X systems with 16GB LPDDR4X, 32 TOPS INT8 and LLM deployment support. Verify the exact board configuration before purchase.

parts.name: Tenstorrent Wormhole n150s PCIe accelerator
parts.host_requirements: x86_64 host, PCIe 4.0 x16, sufficient airflow and host RAM
parts.network: 2x QSFP-DD 400GbE accelerator interconnect plus Warp 100 links
parts.plain_language: This is not a low-watt worker, but it is an important architectural reference: real LLM support, 12GB GDDR6 and accelerator-to-accelerator links hundreds of times faster than ordinary 2.5GbE. It lets the project compare cheap low-power nodes against purpose-built scalable AI silicon without pretending they solve the same problem.
parts.source_notes: Tenstorrent lists n150s at US$999. Official specifications list 12GB GDDR6, 288GB/s bandwidth and up to 160W board power.
